## Static field written by instance method Write to static field from instance method, property, or constructor. --- General approach: avoid writing static mutable state directly inside instance methods/constructors. Encapsulate static mutation behind a static method (or static property setter), and expose read access as needed.

Best fix here (without changing behavior):
In tests/Reactor.Tests/Spec048/V1Protocol/RegBaseTests.cs, inside FirstTouchBaseHandler:

  • Replace public static int CtorCalls; with a private backing field and a read-only public property:
    • private static int _ctorCalls;
    • public static int CtorCalls => _ctorCalls;
  • Add a private static method IncrementCtorCalls() that performs Interlocked.Increment(ref _ctorCalls);
  • Update the instance constructor to call that static method instead of writing the static field directly.

This keeps the test assertion Assert.Equal(0, FirstTouchBaseHandler.CtorCalls); unchanged and preserves thread safety.

## Static field written by instance method Write to static field from instance method, property, or constructor. --- General fix: avoid mutating static fields directly from instance methods/constructors. Route the mutation through a static helper/member so instance code no longer writes static state.

Best fix here (without changing behavior): in each handler class that currently does Interlocked.Increment(ref CtorCalls) inside the instance constructor, introduce a private static method (for example OnCreated) that performs the increment, and call that method from the constructor. This preserves all existing semantics and assertions (CtorCalls still increments once per instance), while satisfying the “instance method directly writes static field” pattern.
